data.title: Nagel: December ECB Rate Increase Would Signal Resolve on Inflation
data.description: Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said another European Central Bank interest-rate increase in December would send a firm message about policymakers’ determination to bring inflation under control, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI TRENDS | DeepSeek’s 100 Billion-Yuan-Level Financing Is Finalized as Registered Capital Rises to 19.918707 Million Yuan
data.description: DeepSeek’s second-round financing, described as being at the 100 billion yuan level, has been finalized. According to Odaily, recent business registration changes show that Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd., DeepSeek’s core operating entity, added Hangzhou Chengyan Enterprise Management Consulting Partnership (Limited Partnership) as a shareholder. The company’s registered capital rose from 16.447496 million yuan to 19.918707 million yuan, an increase of 3.471211 million yuan, or about 21.1%. Hangzhou Chengyan, the new shareholder’s investment vehicle, also updated its registration, increasing its registered capital contribution to 3.438979 billion yuan and adding 31 partners. It now has 32 partners, while Hangzhou Chengce Business Consulting Co., Ltd. remains its executive partner.

data.title: Europe’s Move Away From Russian Fuel Deepens Reliance on Chinese Green Technology
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Europe has sharply cut Russian fuel imports since the conflict in Ukraine and turned to U.S. liquefied natural gas, pushing up energy bills. At the same time, its clean-energy transition has deepened reliance on Chinese technology. Last year, wind and solar power generation in the European Union exceeded generation from fossil fuels.

Chinese equipment supports Europe’s transition but puts pressure on local manufacturers. By company headquarters, China accounted for 79.8% of global solar-module capacity, 91.5% of solar-cell capacity and 92.5% of polysilicon capacity in 2024. China also produces at least 80% of the world’s solar products and lithium-ion batteries. Chinese-made electric vehicles cost about 35% less to manufacture than models made entirely in Europe; Chinese electrolyzers cost less than half as much as European ones, and Chinese wind turbines cost 30% to 45% less.

The EU is considering procurement rules for solar modules, wind turbines and batteries, with negotiations expected to conclude in the coming months. The bloc has already barred Chinese inverters from EU-funded projects and is considering extending the restriction to some grid equipment in projects without EU funding. South Korea has introduced tax credits for domestic solar, wind and battery products, while Japan is subsidizing ultra-thin solar technology. The United States has imposed high tariffs on Chinese solar equipment, electric vehicles and other clean-energy products.

Economists say support for European manufacturers could raise costs and slow clean-energy adoption. Bruegel deputy director Simon Tagliapietra said Europe need not compete in every sector, pointing instead to areas such as cable manufacturing and wind turbines where it retains advantages. He said inexpensive solar panels had helped expand installations, create jobs in installation and maintenance, and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

data.title: Skadden to Hire About 40 Weil Bankruptcy Lawyers, Including 11 Partners
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom will announce on Wednesday that it is hiring about 40 bankruptcy lawyers from Weil, Gotshal & Manges, including 11 partners. Matt Barr, who leads Weil’s bankruptcy practice and is an influential member of its management committee, will head Skadden’s restructuring practice. Barr will remain at Weil through the end of this year before leaving. He had been negotiating with Skadden, as previously reported.

Several other firms, including Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison, had also sought to hire Barr and his team. Weil announced early this fall that it planned to dissolve, and last month decided to wind down. Hundreds of its lawyers must find new jobs. Since the dissolution was announced, Milbank, Kirkland & Ellis, Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, Paul Weiss and Cleary Gottlieb have recruited Weil lawyers.

Weil’s restructuring practice was once a crown jewel of the firm. It helped shape many of the rules and practices of modern bankruptcy law and served as a leading adviser to distressed companies, handling major and complex U.S. restructurings, including those of Lehman Brothers, General Motors and Washington Mutual. Its position in the field has gradually been overtaken by larger rivals, while prominent lawyers have left for other firms. The firm’s overall business growth has stalled in recent years, and more partners have considered leaving, contributing to its decline.

Skadden has long had a strong bankruptcy practice, representing American Airlines, MGM and Charter Communications in related cases, but competitors have taken market share in recent years. Barr became Weil’s global restructuring chair in July. His notable cases include First Brands Group’s complex bankruptcy proceedings, Chapter 11 restructurings for EP Energy, Talen Energy and Fieldwood Energy, and the bankruptcy of CEC Entertainment, the parent company of Chuck E. Cheese.

data.title: Helios, the “Real-Life Theranos,” Claims One-Drop Blood Test Can Predict Health Risks
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Helios emerged from stealth on Wednesday, claiming its blood-testing service can assess health and predict disease risks from a single drop of blood. The 16-month-old startup says its device collects a sample with a light prick and can measure more than 1,000 proteins to assess current health and estimate the risk of conditions including heart failure, blood cancers and Alzheimer’s disease over the next 10 years.

Co-founders Omar Abudayyeh and Jonathan Gootenberg, both 36 and 35 respectively, said Helios raised $2.3 million in seed funding from Y Combinator, venture firm Formation and angel investors. Their third co-founder is Youssef Baroud, a scientist and physician at Massachusetts General Hospital. The founders said prospective investors compared the idea to Theranos but wanted to hear more because they believed it worked.

Helios’s device attaches to the upper arm and collects a drop of blood into a test cartridge. Users send the sealed sample to the company’s Boston laboratory, where protein testing and an AI model are used to assess heart, liver, brain and kidney function and estimate future disease risks. An AI assistant also offers suggestions on diet, lifestyle, supplements and medication. The company says its algorithms draw on more than 80,000 research papers, genetic studies and clinical trials.

Helios plans to offer the test through longevity clinics and concierge doctors in early 2027 for $250 to $600 per test, depending on clinic purchasing volume. It plans to begin direct-to-consumer sales through its website by the end of 2027, but has not set a consumer price.

The company is among businesses developing proteomics tests. Illumina acquired SomaLogic earlier this year, and Thermo Fisher acquired Olink in 2024. Vero Bioscience is also developing a blood test to estimate the biological age of organs. Helios’s founders say proteomics technology differs from Theranos’s, whose claims involved using small blood samples for routine tests.

data.title: IEA Says Data Center Electricity Use Could Double by 2030
data.description: According to CNBC, data centers could consume about 1,000 terawatt-hours of electricity annually by 2030 under the International Energy Agency’s Stated Policies Scenario, roughly double current use as artificial intelligence drives demand. Data center electricity use grew 17% in 2025, compared with 3% growth in global electricity demand. The world’s largest data center operators are expected to spend more than $700 billion in 2026, mostly on new infrastructure. Under the IEA’s Current Policies Scenario, grid spending is projected to rise 75% over the next decade.

data.title: Alibaba's Fiscal Q2 2027 Revenue Reaches 271.5 Billion Yuan, Slightly Above Estimates
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Alibaba (09988.HK) reported revenue of 271.5 billion yuan for fiscal Q2 2027, compared with 247.8 billion yuan a year earlier and market expectations of 269.9 billion yuan. Net profit was 64.5 billion yuan, versus 20.99 billion yuan a year earlier and expectations of 23.52 billion yuan. The company reported an operating margin of 11% and operating profit of 29.1 billion yuan.

data.title: CeFi and DeFi Converge Through Hybrid Crypto Ecosystems
data.description:
Binance Blog published a new article, revealing insights into the growing convergence of centralised finance (CeFi) and decentralised finance (DeFi), and how hybrid models can connect account-based services with public blockchain applications. Published in November 2026, the article describes CeDeFi as an approach that combines CeFi’s accessible interfaces, liquidity and operational safeguards with DeFi’s transparency, permissionless infrastructure and programmable markets. Binance’s ecosystem is presented as an example: its centralised exchange provides custodial trading services, while BNB Chain is a public blockchain that operates independently of the exchange and supports decentralised applications. Wallet integrations and cross-chain infrastructure can help users move assets between these environments. Products including Launchpad and Launchpool link exchange-based participation with projects and tokens that may develop on-chain uses. Binance Wallet provides a self-custody route to third-party applications, while institutional custody and settlement arrangements can offer eligible institutions structured access to exchange liquidity and on-chain opportunities. The article stresses that custody, control and responsibility differ across these services, and that moving between them can change a user’s risk exposure.

The article also examines regulatory considerations, arguing that the treatment of hybrid services depends on the functions performed, the allocation of control and risk, and whether providers actively facilitate financial services or act as intermediaries. It cites the FATF’s 2026 analysis of DeFi arrangements and notes that decentralised technology alone does not determine regulatory treatment. For retail users, moving from a custodial account to a self-custody wallet can provide access to lending applications, but also places greater responsibility on users to verify transactions and assess smart-contract risks. For institutions, custody frameworks and defined workflows may provide a phased path to on-chain strategies, which still carry market, liquidity, operational and protocol risks. The article points to wider convergence through examples including stablecoins, tokenised funds, public-chain settlement and self-custody wallets, while noting that not all such activity is DeFi in the strict sense. It also discusses “TriFi,” a concept bringing together traditional finance, CeFi and DeFi. The article concludes that integrated user experiences need not imply a single regulatory classification: clear boundaries, disclosures and safeguards remain important as users move between financial environments.

data.title: Cook Protocol Launches $SAMANT Meme Token Paired With Tokenized Samsung Electronics Shares
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Cook Protocol recently launched $SAMANT, a meme token paired with tokenized Samsung Electronics shares (SAMSUNGs). Inspired by South Korea’s retail-investor “ant” culture, the token is available for trading in Cook’s Uniswap v4 pool and has a fixed supply of 1 billion.

Each buy or sell in the pool incurs a fee of 2% in SAMSUNGs. The fee allocation is 30% to liquidity providers, 10% to Cook platform fees, 30% to a holder dividend pool, 20% to token buybacks and 10% to project development. Eligible holders can receive proportional dividends without staking, and anyone may trigger a buyback when specified conditions are met.

Cook Protocol says $SAMANT is a meme token and does not grant holders shareholder rights in Samsung Electronics. It also cautions that the token’s price is highly volatile.

data.title: Elon Musk Expects Optimus to Handle Household Chores Within 12–18 Months
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing STAR Market Daily, Elon Musk said in a video interview that he expects the Optimus robot to handle household tasks within 12–18 months, including taking out the trash, washing dishes, and putting them away in cabinets.

data.title: Aelf Says Public Full-Node Service and Aelfscan Faced Thousands of Attacks
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing aelf, the network detected thousands of malicious attacks targeting its public full-node service and Aelfscan over the past two days. Functions dependent on the services have been temporarily suspended while the team works to restore them. The aelf blockchain itself was unaffected and continues producing blocks normally.

data.title: U.S. Gasoline Nears $3.50, Potentially Good News for U.S. President Donald Trump
data.description: According to Jin10, the American Automobile Association (AAA) puts the U.S. average retail gasoline price at about $3.72 per gallon, an eight-month low and 15% below its most recent peak in September. Prices are expected to fall further before the Thanksgiving holiday. The decline reflects a substantial recovery in Middle Eastern crude flows and increased gasoline supply as a byproduct of diesel production, as well as the end of the Northern Hemisphere summer travel season, a seasonal drop in gasoline demand, and rapid growth in electric-vehicle sales. Gasoline nearing the $3.50 threshold is another positive for U.S. President Donald Trump: researchers found that when prices fall below that level, news coverage of gasoline declines sharply and it gradually fades from public discussion.

data.title: California Faces $2 Billion Budget Gap Despite Higher-Than-Expected Tax Revenue
data.description: California is projected to run a $2 billion deficit in the next fiscal year even as tax revenue exceeds expectations, according to a forecast from the Legislative Analyst’s Office released Wednesday. Bloomberg reported.

data.title: My Wallet Launches 1:1 Cross-Chain Swaps After No. 1 WalletConnect WalletGuide Listing
data.description: My Wallet has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe and USDS across eligible supported blockchains, letting users change tokens or networks in one in-app flow with the destination amount fixed before confirmation. The wallet serves more than 10 million users and is listed first in WalletConnect’s WalletGuide, is WalletConnect Certified and connects to more than 80,000 compatible apps, according to BeInCrypto. Powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents and other bridges, the swaps are available for routes above $30 with no exchange-rate spread, slippage or wallet swap commission; applicable network fees are charged separately, and other routes may have different rates and fees. My Wallet also supports native Bitcoin and gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Optimism, in addition to existing gasless support on Solana and TON.

data.title: Variational’s $1.5 Billion Valuation Implies About $47 per Airdrop Point
data.description: Variational raised $110 million in a Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation ahead of a planned airdrop of 32% of its VAR supply. The valuation implies a $480 million airdrop pool, or about $47 per point based on at least 10.2 million points after the November 13 distribution, according to BeInCrypto. The estimate is conditional: Variational has not said whether the valuation applies to the token, and the implied value would decline as more points are issued. The points are weekly rewards for trading on the Omni platform; the program began with 3 million retroactive points and issues 150,000 per week until launch. The airdrop is scheduled to be fully unlocked at launch, while 50% of supply is allocated to the team and investors, locked for 12 months, and 18% to a foundation reserve. Bain Capital Crypto led the round, with Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV, 50T Funds and others participating. Variational said the capital will lift Omni’s open-interest caps and enable hundreds of new stock, index, commodity and FX listings. A precedent is rival Lighter, which raised $68 million at a valuation Fortune reported at around $1.5 billion in November 2025; its founder said the deal included equity and token warrants. Seven weeks later, Lighter launched LIT and airdropped 25% of its supply. Variational’s token launch is due by year-end.
